scope.summary: Lock Tailor implementation and supply inputs: Rust/compiler/crate/model/SDK/config versions and hashes, offline dependency bundle, runtime precedence, profiles/tolerances/fixtures/hardware budgets, adapter identities, DCC profiles and rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Values that require measurement are owned by bounded benchmark/calibration procedures with acceptance rules; the contract does not invent constants before evidence and freezes accepted outputs as versioned profiles.

Profiles separate reference/interactive/final quality, use case, backend, hardware, compiler, driver, asset corpus, units, tolerances, seeds, repeats, timeouts, memory, performance, cancellation, and jitter with content hashes.

The lock registers `hsk.tailor.solver_profile@1` TailorSolverProfileV1 and `hsk.tailor.qualification_profile@1` TailorQualificationProfileV1 with the exact minimum fields in 13.30 [TAI-ACT-008], including version/supersession/status, exact solver lane, comparison kind, numeric/unit policy, device/hardware and fixture hashes, feature flags, measured topology/contact/strain/residual/energy/CCD tolerances, mesh/iteration/frame/time/memory budgets, checkpoint/cancellation/fallback policy, calibration sources, accepted exclusions, actor/event ids, and timestamps.

Runtime and test fixture payloads and executable proof inputs live only under the declared product testdata roots; `.GOV` may retain governance manifests and receipts but no runtime fixture or generated proof payload.
Missing, stale, incompatible, or unmeasured inputs fail dependent work with typed blockers; profile changes invalidate affected baselines and trigger explicit requalification.

The active TailorInterchangeProfile or runtime capability row records exact direction, versions, hashes, supported payloads, losses, unsupported cases, privacy behavior, artifacts and qualification receipts before the action is exposed.

Proof includes successful canonical Rust behavior plus one missing/removed-adapter or unsupported-direction case and demonstrates no partial authority mutation, silent fallback, data loss or false qualification.

The product path is Rust-owned, local and offline: Python/PyTorch, generated executable scripts, cloud services, implicit network access and runtime downloads are prohibited; optional adapters are pinned and removable.
scope.risk_if_missed: Architecture-ready physics can still fail implementation because numerical, hardware, asset, and DCC decisions remain implicit or guessed.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Non-UI contract: typed commands, state, receipts, diagnostics, and TraceProjection provide model/operator observability; the owning native projection is separately contracted.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > Model operation, diagnostics, pillars, and manual

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT must wire the shared internal_diagnostics API for its native, job, device, solver-run, or DCC failure modes with bounded structured evidence.
Long-running, native, or external-process work must register bounded progress and child/process identity with the shared Palmistry watcher; Tailor must not fork a watcher.

risks: Architecture-ready physics can still fail implementation because numerical, hardware, asset, and DCC decisions remain implicit or guessed.
GUI, backend, agent, replay, and manual projections may drift if they do not consume the same typed authority.
minimum_controls: One typed owner and exact stable ids are required.
Negative, concurrent, cancellation, recovery, and no-context proofs are required where applicable.
No validator PASS/FAIL is inferred from this pre-activation contract.

required_changes_before_execution: Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.

requirements: Resolve Principal, AuthenticatedSession and AccessSpace before every resource read or mutation.
Use PostgreSQL RLS/FORCE RLS and ResourceBroker-backed artifact/file handles; UI filtering is never the security boundary.
Derived resources preserve the intersection of source access scopes and must not leak existence through counts, search, previews, logs, traces, caches, diagnostics, exports or model context.
